Looking at this problem, I need to determine the value of $\aleph_0!$, where the factorial of an infinite cardinal $\kappa$ is defined as the number of permutations (bijections) of a set of cardinality $\kappa$.

## Proof

**Definition.** For a cardinal $\kappa$, define $\kappa! = |\{\sigma : \sigma \text{ is a bijection } \kappa \to \kappa\}|$, the cardinality of the permutation group on a set of size $\kappa$.

We prove that $\aleph_0! = 2^{\aleph_0}$.

**Upper bound: $\aleph_0! \leq 2^{\aleph_0}$.**

Every permutation of $\mathbb{N}$ is a function $\mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$, so:
$$\aleph_0! \leq \aleph_0^{\aleph_0}.$$
We show $\aleph_0^{\aleph_0} = 2^{\aleph_0}$:
- $2^{\aleph_0} \leq \aleph_0^{\aleph_0}$ since $2 \leq \aleph_0$ (monotonicity of $\kappa^\lambda$ in the base).
- $\aleph_0^{\aleph_0} \leq (2^{\aleph_0})^{\aleph_0} = 2^{\aleph_0 \cdot \aleph_0} = 2^{\aleph_0}$, using $\aleph_0 \leq 2^{\aleph_0}$ and $\aleph_0 \cdot \aleph_0 = \aleph_0$.

By Cantor–Bernstein, $\aleph_0^{\aleph_0} = 2^{\aleph_0}$, hence $\aleph_0! \leq 2^{\aleph_0}$.

**Lower bound: $2^{\aleph_0} \leq \aleph_0!$.**

We construct an injection from $\mathcal{P}(\mathbb{N})$ into the set of permutations of $\mathbb{N}$.

Partition $\mathbb{N}$ into disjoint pairs $\{2n, 2n+1\}$ for $n \in \mathbb{N}$. For each subset $S \subseteq \mathbb{N}$, define the permutation $\sigma_S : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ by:
$$\sigma_S(2n) = \begin{cases} 2n+1 & \text{if } n \in S \\ 2n & \text{if } n \notin S \end{cases}, \qquad \sigma_S(2n+1) = \begin{cases} 2n & \text{if } n \in S \\ 2n+1 & \text{if } n \notin S \end{cases}.$$

In words: $\sigma_S$ swaps the pair $\{2n, 2n+1\}$ when $n \in S$, and fixes it when $n \notin S$. Each $\sigma_S$ is a bijection (it is its own inverse — an involution).

The map $S \mapsto \sigma_S$ is injective: if $S \neq T$, say $n \in S \setminus T$, then $\sigma_S(2n) = 2n+1 \neq 2n = \sigma_T(2n)$. Therefore:
$$2^{\aleph_0} = |\mathcal{P}(\mathbb{N})| \leq \aleph_0!.$$

**Conclusion.** Combining both bounds via the Cantor–Bernstein–Schröder theorem:
$$\aleph_0! = 2^{\aleph_0}.$$

The factorial of $\aleph_0$ equals the cardinality of the continuum. $\blacksquare$
